title: Centralization vs Decentralization | Principles of Management Ep 26
description:
Who should make the decisions in a growing business? In this animated lesson, Chai Corner now has five outlets and a small head office, but every single decision still waits for Ravi. Outlets call him for cups, for offers, for everything, and by the time he answers, the customers have gone.

You will learn what centralization means (decision-making power kept at the top) and what decentralization means (authority spread to lower levels and units, as a planned system across the whole organization, not just one delegated task). We show why it is a matter of degree, a slider with no real organization at either end, which Henri Fayol called "a question of proportion". Then we cover when to lean central (small firms, uniform rules, a crisis), when to lean decentralized (large, spread out, fast-changing firms), how Ravi splits decisions between head office and his outlet managers, and the advantages and disadvantages of each side.

This is Episode 26 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
